rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This conceptual and problem-solving plan starts with the meaning and structure of the product rule, then moves from a complete example to guided use, independent application, and mixed verification. Each 15-minute session keeps one action prominent and uses attempts to determine whether support is needed.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Build the product rule from the need to differentiate two multiplied functions.
sessions.amountLabel: One product-rule model and one power-rule prerequisite check
contentTargets: Recognize when an expression is a product of two functions
Interpret and state (fg)' = f'g + fg'
completionEvidence: Explain why differentiating each factor and multiplying the results is not the product rule
Apply the rule structure to label the four required parts of one derivative

sessions.title: Follow a Complete Example
sessions.objective: Use the product rule procedure on a polynomial product with guided steps.
sessions.amountLabel: One complete worked example and one closely matched problem
contentTargets: Differentiate each factor using the power rule
Assemble and simplify a product-rule derivative
completionEvidence: Demonstrate each step for differentiating one polynomial product
Solve one closely matched product-rule problem with prompts available

sessions.title: Apply the Rule Independently
sessions.objective: Differentiate products without step prompts and repair any procedural gap.
contentTargets: Choose and apply the product rule independently
Check factor derivatives and algebraic simplification
completionEvidence: Solve two product-rule derivatives without step prompts
Explain and correct any error found in the setup or simplification

sessions.title: Verify Independent Use
sessions.objective: Distinguish product-rule problems from power-rule problems and complete a final application.
sessions.amountLabel: One rule-choice check and one final derivative
contentTargets: Decide whether a problem requires the product rule
Carry out and verify the full derivative independently
completionEvidence: Classify several expressions by whether they require the product rule
Solve and verify one final product-rule problem without assistance

essentialIdeas: An expression is a product of two functions when two functions are multiplied together, so the rule applies to a product form.
For a product fg, the derivative is f'g + fg', which means differentiate each factor separately and add the two resulting parts.
completionEvidence: Identify whether a given expression is a product of two functions.
State the product rule structure correctly from memory.
Distinguish the product rule from multiplying derivatives of the factors.

activities.label: Model
activities.title: Product Form and Rule
activities.body: Review the model and note the two parts. Then match the rule to the product form.

essentialIdeas: An expression is a product of two functions when two functions are multiplied together, so the rule applies to a product form.
For a product fg, the derivative is f'g + fg', which means differentiate each factor separately and add the two resulting parts.

activities.label: Guided Check
activities.title: Spot the Product Rule
activities.body: Name whether the expression is a product of two functions. Then write the product-rule form for it.
activities.concept: Recognize when an expression is a product of two functions
activities.correctAnswer: Yes, it is a product of two functions; use (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
activities.feedback: Correct if you identify two multiplied functions and then give the product-rule structure. A common miss is to multiply the derivatives instead of adding the two product terms.

activities.label: Independent Check
activities.title: State the Rule
activities.body: Answer from memory. Write the product rule in symbols and in words.
activities.correctAnswer: (fg)' = f'g + fg'; differentiate each function separately and add the two parts.
activities.feedback: A complete answer states both the symbolic rule and the idea that each factor is differentiated separately before adding the results. If you wrote a product of derivatives, repair that by keeping the two terms as a sum.

activities.label: Recognition Check
activities.title: Choose the Product Rule
activities.body: Pick the statement that matches the product rule.
choices: Differentiate each factor and add the two products.
Differentiate each factor and multiply the results.
Add the two original functions, then differentiate once.
Differentiate only the first function and leave the second unchanged.
activities.correctAnswer: Differentiate each factor and add the two products.
activities.feedback: The product rule uses two derivative-and-product pieces, then adds them. It does not multiply the derivatives or ignore one factor.

items.essentialIdea: An expression is a product of two functions when two function factors are multiplied.

check.title: Identify function products
check.prompt: Is f(x)g(x) a product of two functions, and why?
check.referenceAnswer: Yes. It is the multiplication of two function factors, f(x) and g(x).
check.feedback: A product has two function factors multiplied together, not added or composed.

items.essentialIdea: (fg)' equals f'g plus fg', combining both factors' derivatives.

check.title: State the product rule
check.prompt: What is the derivative of f(x)g(x)?
check.feedback: Differentiate each factor once, then add the two cross terms.

recognitionCheck.title: Recognize the product rule
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which derivative matches the product rule for f(x)g(x)?
recognitionCheck.feedback: The product rule adds the derivative of each factor times the other factor.
